commands.name: flowleap:patstat-portfolio-analysis (MCP)
commands.description: Resolve an applicant to one harmonized entity and present its patent portfolio with the right caveats.

commands.name: flowleap:patstat-guarded-sql (MCP)
commands.description: Answer an aggregate patent question with agent-written SQL through `patstat_query` (CLI: `flowleap patstat query "<sql>" --question "<question>"`) under the deterministic gate — the one-retry loop. You own the retry: errors carry the exact parser/Postgres detail, fix once, never loop (the 10/min budget is the bound).

commands.name: flowleap:patstat-graph (MCP)
commands.description: Answer "named node and its relationships" questions — citations, family, applicants/inventors, or the path between two patents — with the resolve-first flow: resolve free-form input to an anchor/psn_id once with `patstat_resolve` (CLI: `flowleap patstat graph resolve <input>`), then call the graph tool that matches the question.

EP3477840B1 (University of Maribor, "Welding transformer", granted 2020-05-27) is cited by exactly two documents in PATSTAT 2026 Spring, and both belong to the same Robert Bosch family.

| Citing publication | Applicant | Published | Citation origin |
|---|---|---|---|
| EP3796345A1 | Robert Bosch | 2021-03-24 | SEA, examiner search report |
| CN112530684A | Robert Bosch (罗伯特·博世有限公司) | 2021-03-19 | SEA, examiner search report |

**How they cite it.** Both citations are examiner-origin (SEA), meaning the patent office search found EP3477840 as relevant prior art. Neither was applicant-supplied. The two citing publications share one title, "Welding transformer, method for producing a module for a welding transformer and method for producing a welding transformer", and form a single two-member family. So in invention terms, one Bosch invention cites the Maribor patent, once in Europe and once in China.

**Context.** EP3477840 itself cites nine patent documents, five found by the examiner and four supplied by the applicant, and no non-patent literature. Its family consists of the Slovenian priority filing SI25535A and the Slovenian validation SI3477840T1. No citation ran the other way from Bosch's earlier work into this patent.
